text1: The Wenceslaus is a ship designed to act as a durable core to any fleet.  Being able to act as the flagship of a small anti-piracy fleet, or as a valuable frontline combatant in large scale fleet engagements.  Though lacking significant firepower, it makes up for that in the flexibility of its armament while its ship system keeps it alive in long fleet engagements.

The Hyacinth is a prime example of Iskalan engineering, focusing on long range weapons designed to disable enemy ships, and a large array of weapons designed to shred the enemy to bits at close range.  With the ability to disable enemy ships then move in for the kill, the Hyacinth is capable enough to take on much larger capital ships, whilst still being an agile and nimble vessel able to take on numerous smaller vessels.

The Ladislaus class Hunter-Killer is not a flashy vessel, though able to hold its own against cruisers with its large weapon slot and energy focusing, it has nothing in the way of flashy or unique abilities.  The Ladislaus is a ship designed to get the job done.  The Ladislaus is capable of holding the line, hunting down smaller frigates, or defending and escorting larger capital ships.  Though it is notable in its major sacrifice of hull strength for its speed and firepower, captains of the Ladislaus are recommended to not take direct hits, instead they are recommended to take glancing blows that can be absorbed by the Ladislaus heavy armor.

A unique vessel within the sector, as the Iskalans have few dedicated fighters, preferring larger vessels on par with frigates to act as screens and scouts.  The Eurosia class reflects this doctrine in its ludicrously sized forges designed to build and repair frigates, and the large amount of empty space within the vessel meant to be gutted and fitted with frigate bays.

The Iskalans, due to technical limitations, are unable to build an FTL device small enough to fit a frigate.  The Pelczar class is meant to provide the fuel needed for the larger vessels within the Iskalan fleet, being the smallest class of antimatter fuel carrier built by the Iskalans.

The smallest cargo carrier built by the Iskalans, the Kowalska class is a ship designed to be affordable, efficient, and capable.  Being the smallest, the Kowalska needed to provide an economy of scale at an affordable price that could allow it to corner the market, as most up-and-coming captains would prefer to purchase a smaller and cheaper vessel if given the choice.  This vessel also had the unenviable task of fulfilling military demands on top of this.

The Piotr Class light gunship is a nimble ship designed to use its shimmer core to harass an enemy fleet, forcing the enemy fleet to either accept the assault or detach a part of the fleet to hunt the Piotr.  Both outcomes are ideal, as the Piotr usually comes equipped with weapons capable of dealing high EMP damage, meaning the Piotr can come in behind an enemy vessel and disable their main engines with ease.  Any enemy willing to hunt the Piotr will have to be fast or the subsequent engagement will be a protracted goose hunt as the Piotr is able to outmaneuver most vessels.  The Piotr, however, shares the common trait among all Iskalan vessels in that the internal components are wildly outsized for a vessel of the Piotr’s size.  The result is the Piotr lacking any onboard FTL, making it reliant on larger vessels for transit through space.

According to all known records, the Union of Iskala shouldn’t exist.  No mention of an inhabited planet in the region of Iskala exists within the records of the hegemony or the galatia academy, only basic planetary data can be found.  To some, this shows that the Iskalans are invaders from outside of the sector, but to others affirms the Iskalans story, one told to the first explorers to find Iskala, around the time of the invasions of warlord Loke.  This crisis however prevented most from caring about this newly discovered planet with hundreds of millions of people inhabiting it, except for Tri-Tachyon. Shortly before the Askonia crisis, Tri-Tachyon used the corruption within the Hegemony ranks to bribe an admiral to assist a Tri-Tachyon invasion of Iskala.  Through a hard fought battle which resulted in many deaths, the Union of Iskala repelled the invasion and in the aftermath convinced the other states on Iskala to join the Union.  In the following aftermath Iskala rapidly colonized its surrounding systems and built up a military strong enough to make any power within the sector balk at an attempt of invasion.  

The Union of Iskala is unique in its technology and government.  The Union has a large body of knowledge on terraforming planets and recreating earth-like ecosystems, mostly through the use of nano-machines and genetic manipulation.  These nano-machines also support the best healthcare system in the sector, with the nanomachines providing rapid and easy to use medicine.  This effective medicine is also supported by a large network of Hospitals funded in part by the Catholic Church.  The government is also unique, with a bicameral legislative body, and a Cesarz as the head of state and head of the military. The position of Cesarz is hereditary and passed down from one member of the Vasilenko house to the next. These unique features scare many away from interacting with the Union, not least of all the Luddic Church, to whom the Union is their worst fears made manifest.  To many though, the Union of Iskala is a remarkably stable nation within a largely unstable sector, and there are countless immigrants who move to the Union every year.

“Once an ice planet, Lazurowe Morze has been terraformed into a water world with a comfortable gravity for human habitation.  Though not as favorable for human habitation as Ladnysiez, it sports a sizable population, good tourism, and large cities. Its economy is boosted by its mineral and water exports to Kuznia.  Where the water supports the population and terraforming efforts on the planet.” From Iskalan media records.

“Kuznia is a Desert world with next to no atmosphere, determined to not even be a worthwhile terraforming project.  This however, combined with how close it is to the Swiatana system made it a perfect choice to set up heavy industry reliant on dirty Domain era industrial techniques.  Though dirty, Kuznia is known to produce reliable ships within some of the safest conditions within the sector, Kuznia is home to the largest concentration of immigrants within the Union of Iskala.” From Iskalan media records.
text3: Approaching Kuznia, the local military orbital coordinator hails you and directs you to the orbit your fleet will hold.  As you orbit, you look at the planet below.  Large wind-swept deserts cover the planet; dotted with the occasional oasis, and red plants stradling said oasis.  The largest features on the surface are the massive industrial cities built into the mountains, with massive hangers housing countless freighters hauling materials from the surface up to the enormous orbital shipyards your fleet dances around in orbit. Though the oasis you saw hints at the planet's hopes of becoming habitable one day, and the distinct lack of industrial pollution supports the idea that those goals may one day come true.  The massive industrial parks are quite telling as to the current purpose of the planet.  You eventually decide to travel down to the surface.

text1: “The colonization of Iskala occurred around the time of the collapse of the gate network,and was mired with issues. A Gate was never built within the system, and the terraforming efforts made before the arrival of the colonists failed halfway through.  Iskala was barely habitable, yet the new Iskalan colonists persevered and spent blood sweat and tears to transform the planet into a world that rivals even Gilead.” From the records of Historian Janus Kuberski.
text3: As you approach Iskala, an Iskalan military officer hails you, and after giving you a stern look, orders you to enter the designated orbital lane for incoming vessels.  As you orbit, you look at the surface and the beauty of the planet below.  Rivers lazily meander across the surface, while large polar ice caps cover a large chunk of the planet.  Across the planet, forests of deep green trees cover the surface of the planet.  Though you note large spots of red, seemingly plant life, but of a dark red color forming the boundary between areas of greenery and black earth.  large lakes, with not enough salt to be considered oceans, form at the equator of the planet.  Eventually you decide to land on the planet.
